diagnosis: Genuine regression, not an AC1 supersession: honest-GREEN verify's migration-marked run shows only tests/migrations/test_split_code_migration.py::test_split_migration_round_trips_down_then_up_cleanly (T8/PI1-migration-reversible) failing with psycopg.errors.IdleInTransactionSessionTimeout on the post-reupgrade SELECT in _existing_columns(db_session). Root cause is a test-fixture transaction-handling bug in T8 itself (already independently flagged by the Driver as smell test-cost-spiral): after command.downgrade(cfg, '-1'), the test issues two SELECTs via db_session (_existing_columns + the inventory_code row fetch) without committing or rolling back, leaving db_session's connection in an open read transaction; command.upgrade(cfg, 'head') then runs its ALTER TABLE/DDL over Alembic's own separate connection, which lock-waits on db_session's idle transaction until Postgres's idle_in_transaction_session_timeout kills db_session's connection outright. The prior run's second infra failure (test_split_migration_is_atomic_and_rolls_back_completely_on_failure / T9) is collateral: it shares the same db_session fixture/module and was hit by the same killed-connection fallout, not an independent defect. The split migration's up()/down() logic itself is correct (all 12 other S1 tests pass; T9 passes cleanly on a fresh run once T8's connection is not left hanging). This is a test-authoring defect in T8, not production code, and not behavior AC1 intends to change, so it is not a supersession candidate.
fixDirective: In tests/migrations/test_split_code_migration.py::test_split_migration_round_trips_down_then_up_cleanly, commit (or rollback) db_session immediately after the post-downgrade assertions and before calling command.upgrade(cfg, 'head') the second time, e.g. db_session.commit() right after the 'row = db_session.execute(...)' / assert block for the reconstructed inventory_code, so db_session holds no open transaction while Alembic's separate connection runs the re-upgrade DDL.
